question:
Consider the reaction KI (aq) + PbNO₃ (aq) → 2 KNO₃ (aq) + PbI₂ (s).

This is an example of:
solution:
The correct answer is **__Double Displacement__ __Reaction__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI → PbI2 +2KNO3

__
 
• In the given equation, **Pb(NO3)2** reacts with **2KI **to produce **PbI2 **and **2KNO3**.
 
• In a **double displacement reaction**, elements from **two** different compounds **displace **each other to create **new compounds**. This is exactly what is happening in the equation.
 
• The lead ion **(Pb2+**) in lead nitrate displaces the potassium ion (**K+**) in potassium iodide, and the potassium ion (**K+**) in potassium iodide displaces the lead ion (Pb2+) in lead nitrate.
 
• As a result, lead ends up with iodide to form lead iodide (PbI2) and potassium ends up with nitrate to form potassium nitrate (2KNO3).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combination:**

 
 
• A combination reaction is a type of reaction in which two or more substances (elements or compounds) combine to form a single product.
 
• However, in this provided equation, we have two reactants and two products. Hence, it is not a combination reaction.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition:**
 
 
• A decomposition reaction is characterized by a single compound breaking down into two or more smaller compounds or elements.
 
• The given chemical equation does not depict this type of reaction as we start with two reactants which form two new products.
